# Fixed-destination earliest arrival under a single trip cancellation

Use a real timetable and controlled cancellation scenarios. Filter the 19 November 2026 MBTA feed to rail routes of GTFS types 0 and 1 in service on Friday 20 November 2026. Include consecutive same-trip legs departing at or after 07:00 and arriving by 09:00. Collapse child stops to their immediate parent station. Retain positive-duration legs between distinct stations. Treat all such legs as independently boardable and alightable, with zero transfer time at a shared station, regardless of platform. This projected segment network measures an exact timetable optimization problem. It omits walking, boarding restrictions, additional transfers, and accessible-platform transitions. An unreachable result applies within the two-hour network and horizon.

For each station combine events sharing a timestamp into one vertex. Add directed waiting arcs and timed ride arcs. All arcs strictly increase time. A query starts at a station's first event on or after a requested departure and minimizes arrival time at a fixed target. Return a witness for finite answers, including every selected ride leg. Allow waiting at origin. Select four distinct targets by stable lexicographic order after hashing station IDs with the prefix "target:". For each target use 128 origin/time requests deterministically sampled with replacement, source distinct from target, seed 4202. Use the same queries for all methods. Study 48 separately simulated single-trip cancellations, selected by SHA-256 order over active trip identifiers with prefix "trip:". All trips are restored between scenarios. These cancellations are hypothetical. Real service disruptions and another agency/period remain reserved.

Candidate precomputes each destination's exact earliest-arrival dynamic program on the acyclic event graph. Removing a trip only initiates repair where the stored witness used a removed arc. Recompute the best surviving outgoing arc in reverse time order. Propagate to a predecessor only when its chosen successor's arrival value worsens. The handling of equal-valued alternative successors is part of correctness. Undo changed values and successors for the next scenario. Compare (1) forward connection scan per request, (2) full destination-profile recomputation by reverse dynamic programming, (3) exact cached-path invalidation followed by a forward connection scan for each affected request, and (4) a matched incremental repair which schedules every predecessor when its successor's value worsens. Where feasible, add a distinct published incremental algorithm before any confirmation. All methods must output actual ride witnesses and identical optimal arrival times or certified unreachability on every request. Independently recompute optimum distances on the event graph and verify endpoints, transfers and cancellation exclusions for every emitted witness.

Measure single-core steady-clock batch latency including applying the cancellation, solving all requests, producing route lists and restoring the mutable state. Report one-time setup separately and amortized at 48 updates. Take the median of five timed executions per scenario and method in shuffled order, then the nearest-rank 95th percentile across scenarios. A development advance requires at least 10% lower p95 and geometric-mean batch latency than each comparator and exact outcomes throughout. The development screen does not qualify a paper. A claim requires an untouched independent period/operator, clustered inference, competitive implementations and proof under the registered conditions. These results concern a fixed-destination teaching-trip query batch; they cannot establish runtime for heritage itinerary optimization with scoring or other constraints.
